canonical.title: Critical Connections in a Network (Bridges)
canonical.sourceFilePath: 13. Graphs/6. Other Algorithms/01. Bridges in graph.cpp

narrative.title: Flagging the Single Points of Failure
narrative.scenario: A datacentre's redundant links form a mesh, but some links are load-bearing: cut one and part of the cluster goes dark. Auditors call these bridges, and Tarjan's sweep finds them in one pass — a link is critical exactly when the subtree beyond it can never climb back to an earlier-discovered node.
narrative.inputFormat: An integer n (servers 0..n-1) and a list connections where [a, b] is an undirected link.
narrative.outputFormat: Return all critical links as pairs, in any order.

testCases.explanation: The 0-1-2 triangle is self-sustaining; only the spur to server 3 is load-bearing.
With one link and two servers, cutting it isolates both — maximally critical.

hintLevels: Level 1: A bridge's removal splits the graph — no alternative path can exist around it.
Level 2: Record discovery times and the lowest reachable time; compare child's low against parent's tin.
Level 3: Skip the parent edge explicitly (once per undirected pair) or every two-node link looks like a bridge.
